articles.title: Labour poised for tax raid on landlords – press report
articles.summary: The Telegraph assesses the tax options
articles.ai_summary:
- Labour is reportedly considering a major tax overhaul targeting landlords, raising concerns in the property market.  
- Analysts predict significant implications for rental yields as the party evaluates various tax options to generate revenue.

articles.title: Landlord sell-off is a myth, according to think tank
articles.summary: The think tank disputes the findings of agents, analysts and professional bodies
articles.ai_summary:
- A think tank disputes claims from agents and analysts that a significant sell-off of rental properties by landlords is occurring.  
- The report challenges the prevailing narrative, suggesting that current trends may not reflect an actual exodus from the rental market.

articles.title: Renters Rights Act leads to “phenomenal” surge in rent guarantors
articles.summary: Landlords are restricted in taking more than one month rent's upfront
articles.ai_summary:
- The Renters Rights Act has triggered a significant increase in demand for rent guarantors, reflecting new limitations on landlords regarding upfront rent payments.  
- With landlords now restricted to collecting only one month's rent upfront, tenants are seeking more financial security through guarantors.

articles.title: Shock tax hit for landlords with high value properties?
articles.summary: Landlords with high value properties in a portfolio may be caught by what looks like an expansion of the mansion tax. The Tomes reports that Labour may extend its Mansion Tax to properties worth over £1.5m ‌from  the current £2m. £2m is the current threshold at which owners will from 2028 pay the High Value Council […]
articles.ai_summary:
- Labour plans to lower the mansion tax threshold, potentially impacting landlords with properties valued over £1.5m instead of the current £2m, starting in 2028.  
- This move could significantly increase tax liabilities for high-value property owners, raising concerns among landlords.

articles.title: Landlords quitting at highest rate for a decade
articles.summary: Landlords are exiting the lettings market at the highest rates for at least 10 years. Figures released this afternoon by respected property consultancy TwentyCi show 562 properties per day are leaving the private rental sector in Q3 of 2026 so far. That’s a total of 44,000 at the time of writing.  At this point last […]
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords are leaving the UK rental market at the fastest pace in a decade, with 562 properties exiting daily in Q3 2026.  
- A total of 44,000 properties have been removed from the private rental sector so far this year, causing significant market shifts.

articles.title: NRLA says Buy To Let must work alongside Build To Rent
articles.summary: The new Build To Rent (BTR) arm of the National Residential Landlords Association has produced figures emphasising the significance of the BTR sector. NRLA Living says BTR has delivered an average of 61% of new homes built across eight of the UK’s leading regeneration areas over the past decade, despite accounting for under 2% of […]
articles.ai_summary:
- The NRLA highlights that Build To Rent (BTR) has contributed to 61% of new homes in key UK regeneration areas over the past decade.  
- The association emphasizes the need for Buy To Let (BTL) to coexist with the growing BTR sector to enhance housing solutions.

articles.title: Lloyds Bank now owns and manages thousands of private rental properties
articles.summary: It's latest addition comes from a deal with a house builder
articles.ai_summary:
- Lloyds Bank expands its portfolio by acquiring and managing thousands of private rental properties through a recent partnership with a house builder.  
- This strategic move marks a significant shift in the bank's involvement in the property rental market.

articles.title: Labour council wants landlords to help it out of its housing crisis
articles.summary: A Labour local authority is inviting landlords to hear about what it calls “the benefits of working with the council.” Reading council is to reveal details of its rent guarantee scheme, and the incentives available to landlords who sign up to it. A council spokesperson says: “The council has worked closely with Reading landlords for […]
articles.ai_summary:
- Reading Council is actively seeking partnerships with landlords to address the local housing crisis, promoting a rent guarantee scheme to boost incentives for participation.
- The Labour-led council emphasizes the benefits of collaboration, aiming to enhance housing availability and support for both landlords and the community.

articles.title: Government may ease controversial holiday lets thresholds
articles.summary: A consultation is underway which may ease pressure on holiday let landlords. Currently, holiday let properties must be available to rent for at least 252 days a year and actually booked for a minimum of 182 days to qualify for business rates. Properties that don’t reach the occupancy thresholds are usually treated as domestic second […]
articles.ai_summary:
- The UK government is considering relaxing occupancy thresholds for holiday let landlords, currently set at 252 days available and 182 days booked to qualify for business rates.  
- A public consultation aims to alleviate pressure on landlords, potentially changing the treatment of properties that fall short of these requirements.

articles.title: NRLA joins landlord briefing on Renters Rights Act next week
articles.summary: Another council is to brief private landlords on the new Renters Rights Act. Cheshire West and Chester council is holding a forum on the issue on Thursday September 24, organised in partnership with the National Residential Landlords Association (NRLA). Samantha Watkin from the NRLA will discuss how the new landlord database will work. Officers from […]
articles.ai_summary:
- Cheshire West and Chester council, in collaboration with the NRLA, will host a landlord briefing on the new Renters Rights Act on September 24.  
- NRLA's Samantha Watkin will outline the functionalities of the upcoming landlord database during the forum.

articles.title: Council to use “intelligence” held in new landlord database
articles.summary: The council says it wants to be a national leader in enforcement
articles.ai_summary:
- The council aims to become a national leader in enforcement by leveraging intelligence from its new landlord database.  
- Enhanced data insights will drive targeted actions against non-compliant landlords to improve rental standards.

articles.title: More rental properties listed as Bills Included
articles.summary: But it's not the same in every region
articles.ai_summary:
- A growing number of rental properties in the UK are being listed with bills included, attracting more tenants seeking convenience.  
- However, the trend varies significantly across different regions, highlighting localized housing market differences.

articles.title: New health and safety guide issued to landlords by government
articles.summary: The updated guide applies only to England
articles.ai_summary:
- The UK government has released an updated health and safety guide specifically for landlords in England.  
- This new guidance emphasizes the importance of compliance to ensure tenant safety and welfare.

articles.title: New HMO clampdown is seeking landlord views
articles.summary: The council wants all HMOs to require planning consent in future
articles.ai_summary:
- The council is proposing that all Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) must obtain planning consent moving forward.  
- They are currently seeking feedback from landlords on this new clampdown.

articles.title: Cannabis farms send landlords’ profits up in smoke
articles.summary: Insurance claims by property owners have soared
articles.ai_summary:
- Property owners face soaring insurance claims due to illegal cannabis farms, significantly impacting their profitability.
- Landlords are grappling with rising costs and risks associated with property damage linked to cannabis cultivation.

articles.title: Renters Rights Act backfires as landlords reject more tenants
articles.summary: Is the answer to say No more often? Or to have improved vetting procedures?
articles.ai_summary:
- The Renters Rights Act is prompting landlords to increasingly reject prospective tenants in response to new regulations.  
- Landlords are considering stricter vetting processes as a potential solution to mitigate risks associated with the Act.

articles.title: Flats falling out of favour in rental hotspots
articles.summary: Flats are most common - but houses are arguably the most popular
articles.ai_summary:
- Rental demand is shifting from flats to houses, as homes gain popularity in key hotspots.  
- Despite flats being the most prevalent rental option, they are losing favor among tenants.

articles.title: Mortgage rates up again ahead of Bank of England decision
articles.summary: Moneyfactscompare has made a detailed survey of the current market
articles.ai_summary:
- Mortgage rates are on the rise once more, creating uncertainty for potential homeowners ahead of the Bank of England's forthcoming decision.  
- A recent survey by Moneyfactscompare highlights significant shifts in the current mortgage market landscape.

articles.title: Landlords prefer local investment as buy to let strategy shifts
articles.summary: This is according to a bank's survey
articles.ai_summary:
- A recent bank survey reveals that landlords are increasingly favoring local investments over distant properties in their buy-to-let strategies.  
- This shift reflects changing market dynamics and a focus on financial stability within the rental sector.
